newsitem.title: PERU: Peru plans May auction of two Centromin mines.
newsitem.headline: Peru plans May auction of two Centromin mines.

text.p: Peru's state-owned mining firm Centromin plans to auction off its Andaychagua and San Cristobal mines as a single firm in May, a company spokesman said Thursday.
"We have united the two production units to create Empresa Minera Mahrtunel, which will be offered to private investors in May," the Centromin spokesman told Reuters.
Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc.
"Both mines are very close to one another and some 50 kilometers (30 miles) from the smelting and refining complex at La Oroya," he said.

La Oroya, Centomin's most important asset, is slated to be sold April 14. The complex is located in Peru's central Andes some 3,700 yards (meters) above sea level and 120 miles (190 kms) east of Lima.

Centromin recently sold the Yauliyacu mine to the local firm Casapalca and transferred other important mineral deposits to two Canadian groups: Barrick Gold Corp and a consortium comprised of Rio Algom Ltd and Inmet Mining Corp.
Centromin is in the process of being privatized in a piecemeal fashion, including the planned sale of mines, a refinery, hydroelectric centrals and polymtallic mineral deposits.
